methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: Richmond Times-Dispatch opinion piece frames Virginia's AI challenge as small-business adoption, not infrastructure—signaling that concentration in data center buildout isn't translating to distributed capability or entrepreneurial fluency across the commonwealth's economic base.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches AI training program for workplace professionals - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College launching workplace AI training represents regional capacity-building outside NoVA/Richmond hubs, signaling potential for peer-driven skill development that could distribute deep capability beyond traditional tech corridors.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops led by Norfolk native directly target the technology gap through grassroots education, exemplifying distributed peer learning that builds local fluency rather than platform dependency or metro concentration.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU partnership with AI Ready RVA deepens Richmond's institutional AI capacity through university-community collaboration, but concentration in metro anchor institutions risks reproducing hub-spoke patterns unless mechanisms diffuse knowledge to surrounding regions.

signals.title: Press Release: Morgan Griffith Announces HHS Grant to Virginia Tech for AI Health Care Research - Quiver Quantitative
signals.signal_reading: Federal HHS grant to Virginia Tech for AI health research concentrates deep technical capability in established research institution, reinforcing New River Valley as specialized AI hub while broader question remains whether this expertise transfers to regional healthcare providers and rural communities.
